top_choice_rationale: P004 (B019: Autor, Hanson, Dorn) is the contribution whose central claim, persistent local adjustment costs after trade and technology shocks, rests on transparent quasi-experimental designs that others have re-examined at length. The credit for the China-shock evidence is concentrated in a joint Autor-Dorn-Hanson body of work. A citation limited to empirical analysis of adjustment avoids the task-theory attribution problems. Magnitude and persistence are still debated, and I may overweight identification, so this is a close call. P002 (B001) comes next for its clean two-person attribution and durable framework. P001 (B020) follows because its empirical reach is the widest, but the credit boundary with Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum is unresolved. P003 (B016) ranks lower because its identification is weaker and it overlaps thematically with the 2024 prize. No award is last because every proposal describes a mature, substantial contribution.
